Histopathological examination of skin biopsies showed slight acanthosis, focal parakeratosis, minimal and multifocal vacuolar degeneration of the basal layer, focal exocytosis of sparse lymphocytes, mild superficial perivascular and lichenoid lymphocytic infiltrates, and multifocal melanin‐laden macrophages with golden‐brown granules located both perivascularly and in other areas of the dermis (pigmentary incontinence) (Figure 2). She reported no family history of dermatological disorders, no recent travel, infections, or changes in medications.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Low-power esophageal squamous mucosa with band-like basal infiltrate in case titled Pityriasis Lichenoides Chronica of Esophagus, attributed to PLC. B: Same low-power histology as A showing band-like lymphocytic infiltrate attributed to esophageal PLC. C: Medium-power view with acanthosis, intraepithelial lymphocytosis and apoptotic keratinocytes in esophageal PLC case. D: High-power view showing prominent apoptotic/necrotic keratinocytes attributed to esophageal pityriasis lichenoides chronica.

in_text_mentions: n consisted of a few, tiny, tan-pink esophageal mucosal fragments. Microscopic evaluation revealed multiple fragments of esophageal squamous mucosa showing a band-like inflammatory infiltrate (Figure 1A), with diffuse lymphocytes exocytosis (intraepithelial lymphocytosis), acanthosis, basal cell hyperplasia with prominent apoptotic keratinocytes identified (Figures 1B-1D). The inflammatory infiltrate was composed predominantly of CD3+ T-lymphocytes with scattered plasma cells and macrophages.
